name: Discofox octave bass
rationale: The defining Schlager / Discofox bass: the root on every beat and the octave above on every off-beat, so the bass bounces against the four-on-the-floor kick. Schlager currently borrows the EDM bass generators, which never play this. Four takes: straight octaves, octaves with a fifth on beat 3 for movement, a root-fifth-octave walk, and a lighter verse version with quarter notes and an octave pickup into each bar.

name: Off-beat house bass
rationale: House and EDM bass that sits between the kicks: short notes on every off-beat, leaving the downbeat to the kick drum, which keeps the low end clean and makes the groove pump. EDM's soft bass bank has only three patterns. Three takes: plain off-beats, off-beats that jump to the octave at the end of each bar, and a rolling version with two 16ths after each kick.

name: 808-style sustained bass
rationale: Modern hip-hop and trap bass behaves like an 808: long, sustained roots that ring under the beat, retriggered on syncopated 16ths that line up with a typical trap kick, with the odd jump to the fifth or octave for a hook. Urban's own bass generator follows the drums but has no long-note style, and its fallback bank is small. Three takes from sparse to busier.
